reconciliation_notes:
Both verifiers recommended GOLD/high-trust and independently confirmed the two load-bearing memory numbers (44GB on-wafer SRAM, 21 PB/s aggregate BW) and the 125 PFLOPS device peak plus 900k cores. I set the final twin to SILVER rather than GOLD because the compute-peak field the experiment actually reads is per-instance peak_macs_per_s (6.944e10), which is back-derived (SILVER), and the per-core microarchitecture (matrix_unit, clock) is BRONZE and does not reconcile with the device top-line. Memory tiers are genuinely GOLD, so this is a conservative, honest floor between the researcher's SILVER and the verifiers' GOLD.

Disputed fields resolved: (1) matrix_unit - adopted the two verifiers' higher-trust WSE-3 finding of an 8-wide FP16 SIMD FMAC lane, encoded as [1,1,8], correcting the researcher's WSE-2-era [1,1,4]; kept BRONZE because it is a dataflow SIMD lane, not a systolic [m,n,k] tile. (2) clock_hz - both verifiers showed Cerebras does not publish a WSE-3 clock and the 'vendor_whitepaper' label was wrong; kept 1.1 GHz as a directional value but downgraded to BRONZE/estimate. (3) device_peak label - value 1.25e17 is correct but Cerebras quotes it as FP16, not BF16; recorded compute_dtype='fp16' (dtype_bytes=2 unaffected). (4) tdp_w and per_core_power - 23 kW is CS-3 system power (cooling/IO/host), not the wafer die; marked BRONZE and annotated; did not emit a per-core power field since it would be a naive system/core division. (5) energy_pj_per_byte and line_bytes - not published; kept as explicit BRONZE modeling estimates (1.0 pJ/B, 4 B word).

RB-05 structure: HBM-less chip, so backing role='sram' (44GB @ 21PB/s, hbm_bandwidth_bps/hbm_capacity_bytes=0) -> reuse role='sram' (48KB/core local, instances=900000) -> compute leaf (dataflow FMAC, instances=900000). Experiment-read fields all present: bandwidth_bps, capacity_bytes, energy_pj_per_byte, peak_macs_per_s, instances, matrix_unit, dtype_bytes. arch_note flags 'no HBM; on-wafer resident; no spill cliff' as the intended contrast result.
unresolved: Per-core datapath vs device peak: 125 PFLOPS FP16 over 900k cores at 1.1 GHz implies ~63 MAC/cycle/core, which contradicts BOTH the public 4-wide (WSE-2) and 8-wide (WSE-3) FP16 FMAC descriptions. per_instance_mac_s is back-derived from the GOLD device peak for twin self-consistency; the true WSE-3 per-core width/clock is not publicly reconciled. matrix_unit [1,1,8] and clock 1.1 GHz are therefore nominal BRONZE placeholders.
WSE-3 core clock frequency is not officially published by Cerebras (1.1 GHz is a WSE-2-era/community estimate).
Wafer-only (die) power is undisclosed; only the ~23 kW full CS-3 system figure exists, so tdp_w conflates system vs device.
On-chip SRAM energy (pJ/byte) and memory line/burst size are not published; 1.0 pJ/B and 4 B are generic modeling assumptions (BRONZE).
device peak is quoted by Cerebras as FP16, not BF16 - numerically identical 2-byte path but a semantic dtype note, not a verified BF16 spec.
